recruit_text.greeting: Water first, then we'll talk about whatever you came here to say.
recruit_text.backstory: Twenty-eight years guiding caravans out of Zagora, across ground where a wrong turn costs a camel and a second wrong turn costs a man. He reads sand the way a sailor reads water. The spirits of the land here needed an introduction, and then settled into something he finds entirely familiar: a long relationship with a landscape that would kill him on a technicality.
recruit_text.before:
Camels, tourists, and a route his father and his father's father walked before him.

He raised four children on it with his wife Khadija. Three are grown. The fourth, Nour, was nine.
recruit_text.now:
Freewind Post, between caravan runs across the canyons of Thousand Needles and the Shimmering Flats, where the goblins pay for a man who gets cargo across intact.

He gets it across. He's refused two contracts over the water allowance, and both parties came back with a better one.
recruit_text.forward:
A route across the Shimmering Flats that a caravan can use in summer, when nobody can cross now. There's a way through and he has most of it.

Finishing it means four more seasons of walking, and he has the seasons.

stages.stranger: I'm Driss, a shaman, and before that a desert guide. Drink some water first, please, and then we'll talk. I never let anybody in my care run short of water.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Zagora, in Morocco, at the edge of the Sahara. My father and grandfather guided caravans across the desert, and I learned the routes on a camel before I could read. When the tourists came I guided them too, first on camels and later in two old Land Cruisers I kept running with my own hands, for twenty-eight years.
stages.companion: I was under a truck in the desert fixing an axle, and when I slid out I was on salt flats I'd never seen, with this wrench still in my hand. I asked the land for permission in my own language, and something answered. My wife is Khadija. We have four children. Youssef, Amina and Hamza are grown. Nour was nine.
stages.friend: Nour came long after the others, and she was the light of our house. She'd be twelve now. I tell stories about her by the fire because if I stop telling them I'm afraid I'll forget her laugh. The last stretch of my summer route needs water, and there's none on any map. I think there's a spring under the salt. Will you help me find it, inshallah?
stages.sworn: On the second night of the first summer crossing, I heard a girl laughing at the back of the caravan, and I knew the laugh. It was Nour, twelve now, and Khadija with her. They'd been waiting in a Moroccan camp in Tanaris for two years, unable to cross the Flats in summer. My route brought them. I carried her the rest of the way on my shoulders, though she says she's too old. That night I made mint tea for everybody.

moments.prompt: He hands you a waterskin before anything else and waits.

options.reply: Good, now we can talk. Yallah, I'll come with you.
Everybody's thirsty, they just don't know it yet. Come back when you've learned that.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help him find the spring under the salt.

options.reply: Bismillah, let's go. We'll leave at dawn, before the heat, and we'll carry plenty.

options.text: Why does the route matter so much?
options.reply: Because somebody's waiting on the other side of the Flats. I'd want somebody to come for me.

lines.bored_warning: The land has nothing new to tell us on this circle. Let's find a road we haven't walked.
lines.leaving_good: That was a good journey, and nobody went thirsty. I'll be at Freewind Post, with the tea on.
lines.leaving_bored: There are caravans at Freewind Post that need a guide, and this isn't going anywhere. I'll go to them.
lines.after_wipe: Sit, everybody, and drink something. Then we'll talk about where we went wrong.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep falling in here, under all this rock where no air moves. I'll take you to the end of this one, then I need open sky.
lines.wipe_leave: It's done, and I'm going back to Freewind Post. The desert will teach us, inshallah.
lines.zone_warning: This place is like the deep desert in August. Brave people die there, and so do foolish ones. Let's go back.
lines.zone_leave: I said it was the deep desert in August, and I meant it. I'll be at Freewind Post.
lines.gear_refuse: Travel with me a while longer first, my friend, and then ask.
lines.gear_taken: It's yours, then. I've crossed the Sahara with less.
lines.gear_short: There's a gap in my gear still. Bring water before you bring armour, but bring both.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's beautiful work. Shukran, thank you.
lines.back: The caravans are all home safe. Drink something first, and then tell me the road.
lines.send_word: Driss has sent word from Freewind Post. His caravans are home safe and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Walking away like that wasn't good of me. Sit, drink some tea, and I'll tell you why. After that I want to hear you.
lines.neglect: You've been gone a long time. I kept water for you anyway.
lines.asked_to_stay: Yallah, one more journey. Then the caravans.
lines.on_break: Driss is back at Freewind Post, guiding caravans. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

zone_arrive.text: Check your water before anything else. This ground will take it from you without asking.

town_arrive.text: My father could smell water from a mile off. I've only got about half of that, but there's a good well in this town somewhere.

boss_down.text: The land answered me just then. That part I'm still not used to.

dungeon_clear.text: No air moving in there at all, and I hated it. Let's get under the sky.
